requests.what: Add a named check to reference/verify.py: on every simply laced type of rank at most 8, the state graph of Kostant's game over all starting cities equals the Hasse diagram of the positive roots. The page could then call the statement verified; for now it gives the argument from F2 instead.

Unchanged and not relied on: a data-out or attribute naming the board and node shown, so that a challenge check could accept several right answers (for example 'a node of D5 where the recipe fails') without matching T12's caption text.

openQuestions: SPEC 2.16 (Quiver representations) and SOURCES 11.3 [BGP73] compress Theorem 1.1. Proposed wording: 'for an indecomposable representation other than the simple one at that node, the dimensions change by exactly the mutation rule'. Without it the statement is false for the simple representation at a sink. SPEC.md was not edited.
SPEC Appendix D main correction 3 and 2.4(b) say R_i=S_i^T are 'two different matrices'. Proposed: 'at any node joined to another'. On A1, and at an isolated node, S_i = R_i.
SPEC 2.7 F11 'Their number is det C-1': propose 'on a connected board'. On A1+A1, which classify calls finite component by component, both nodes are minuscule but det C - 1 = 3.

SPEC 3 M8 beat 6 and 2.18 call the 248 the smallest representation of E8 with no label. The lesson now calls it 'a standard fact of Lie theory'. A source in SOURCES.md, or an explicit label, would settle it.
SPEC 2.16 states the Hasse diagram of Kostant's game with no label; see the request to the owner.

handoff: All twelve findings are fixed in the two MDX files, and each has at least one M8.spec.ts assertion shown to fail on the reviewed text (a soft-assertion scratch revert, log in the scratch directory). The page now calls verified only what verify.py checks, with ranges. The Hasse diagram and the CS_i/R_i identities are given with short arguments instead, and the owner is asked for a verify.py check. Two challenges were replaced by single-answer ones on E6 and D5, because T12's caption check accepts only one state; the review's D5/E7 suggestions have several answers. The SPEC text that has the same compressions is proposed under openQuestions and was not edited.
